title: AL20 Local Development Strategy 2023–2027
intro: EDL means Estrategia de Desarrollo Local; EDLL adds LEADER. This library summarises the relevant content of the approved AL20 strategy. Source references are supporting evidence for a self-assessment, not certification or automatic point awards. NPL codes and innovation numbering follow the strategy; Women, Youth, Trade, Heritage and OT labels are library reference identifiers.

topics.title: Prioritised needs addressable through LEADER
topics.summary: All 50 NPL needs, in the strategy’s original priority order. The separate NPNL list is not included as a list addressable through LEADER. The published ranking values do not become CO.1 points.

topics.title: Innovative sectors: none designated
topics.summary: Section 4.4 explicitly opts for innovative themes and integrated aspects instead of designating innovative economic sectors. This edition therefore provides no sector list for IN.1.1. Do not relabel general economic opportunities as designated innovative sectors; a positive claim needs documented GDR clarification.

topics.title: Five explicitly innovative themes
topics.summary: Section 4.4 lists these five themes. Check the scope and conditions of the operation, not only similarity of its title.

topics.title: Twelve explicitly innovative aspects
topics.summary: Section 4.4 lists these twelve integrated aspects. Certification, income, staffing, professional-supervision and geographic conditions remain part of the descriptions.

topics.title: Activities and interests recorded in women’s consultation
topics.summary: The diagnosis records the following requests and interests. These are faithful summaries of consultation findings, not a newly invented eligibility schedule. IG.8.2 and IG.11.7 still require an explanation of how the proposed activity or event addresses the documented demand.

topics.title: Documented needs relevant to inclusion
topics.summary: The diagnosis notes limited provision for people at risk of exclusion (page 191). Related prioritised needs concern care, health/education, reconciliation, disability and tolerance. Explain which at-risk population is served and its specific need; these broad needs are not automatic proof of DRI.3.3.

topics.title: Youth needs recorded in consultation
topics.summary: The diagnosis and youth-impact report record these needs. Select only the references that the operation actually addresses, and explain that connection.

topics.title: Traditional trades explicitly identified
topics.summary: Opportunity O(3.12) names carpentry, stone working, breadmaking and wineries. The list is illustrative, not an exhaustive approved menu of crafts or dishes. No named list of traditional dishes is established here; other claims need an exact strategy passage or GDR clarification.

topics.title: Rural heritage identified in the strategy
topics.summary: The diagnosis identifies these heritage resources and landscapes. NPL3 calls for conservation, enhancement and dissemination of rural heritage; NPL18 covers heritage-based tourism. The operation must explain its contribution, rather than claiming points for location alone.

topics.title: Cross-cutting objectives of the strategy
topics.summary: The prioritisation method and dedicated impact reports identify gender equality, rural youth and climate action. PS.1.2 additionally requires actual membership in an organisation whose objectives include the relevant objective; a project theme alone does not establish membership. Financial percentages on page 527 are programme targets, not this criterion’s point values.

items.label: Attract residents by promoting municipal assets and proximity services
items.summary: The operation develops all or part of an initiative attracting residents through the municipality’s values and proximity-service offer.

items.label: Integrate new residents in municipalities at risk of depopulation
items.summary: The operation develops all or part of an initiative integrating newcomers in municipalities at risk of depopulation.

items.label: Senior cohousing services
items.summary: The operation develops cohousing services for older people.

items.label: Age-friendly municipality certification plans
items.label_es: Comunidades amigables con las personas mayores
items.summary: The operation develops all or part of a plan for certification within the WHO Global Network for Age-friendly Cities and Communities.

items.label: Child-friendly municipality certification plans
items.summary: The operation develops all or part of a municipal Child Friendly Cities certification plan.

items.label: Older people’s residences organised into living units
items.summary: Create, expand or improve older people’s residences using post-COVID living-unit criteria.

items.label: Mobile or itinerant proximity services
items.summary: Businesses guarantee proximity services in municipalities at risk of depopulation through mobile or itinerant provision.

items.label: Documented income from carbon-sink capacity
items.summary: The operation must demonstrate that carbon-sink capacity generates one of its income sources. Planting trees alone does not establish this condition.

items.label: Attract businesses and remote workers
items.summary: Demonstrably facilitate the location of administrative, intellectual or artistic businesses or remote workers in municipalities at risk of depopulation.

items.label: Regenerative-agriculture certification application
items.summary: Demonstrate an application for quality certification of regenerative agricultural activity. Footnote 1 identifies Regenerative Organic Certified (ROC). A generic regenerative claim is insufficient.

items.label: Professionally supervised urban liveability plans
items.summary: Plans for the main settlements’ urban centres must involve or be supervised by architecture professionals, individually or through professional bodies. Footnotes include mobility, public-space use, leisure areas and urban/periurban trails.

items.label: Business relocation tied to resident employment
items.summary: Relocate a business establishment or part of a business, affecting more than one worker resident in municipalities considered at risk of depopulation.

items.label: Certified, communicated carbon or water footprint
items.summary: Certify and communicate the carbon and/or water footprint to customers or service users; certification must demonstrate efficiency in the greenhouse-gas balance and/or water footprint.

items.label: Integrated Camino Mozárabe tourism services
items.summary: Develop integrated tourism services for the Camino Mozárabe as it crosses the territory.

items.label: Themed tourism through cooperation
items.summary: The operation develops tourism themes while promoting cooperation between different agents.

items.label: Precision agriculture with territorial limitations
items.summary: Precision agriculture, such as drones and sensors, applies in low-agricultural-production municipalities. In Dalías and Berja the text restricts it to traditional, low-technology agriculture.

items.label: Agricultural logistics and auxiliary services
items.summary: The strategy identifies agricultural logistics and auxiliary services as innovative in low-agricultural-production municipalities, excluding Dalías and Berja.

items.label: Equality, shared care responsibilities and prevention of gender violence
items.summary: Consultation responses call for awareness activities on equality, shared responsibilities and gender violence.

items.label: Active leisure and cultural activities for women
items.summary: Consultation responses request better active-leisure opportunities, cultural activities and access to leisure services. The strategy does not prescribe named classes or an exhaustive event schedule.

items.label: Create and renew women’s associations
items.summary: Requests include creating associations, access to finance, reactivation, modernisation and generational renewal.

items.label: Visibility, recognition and cooperation among women
items.summary: Consultation calls for activities recognising women’s role in the territory and cooperation between women.

items.label: Vocational qualifications and tailored training
items.summary: Requests include vocational training, professional accreditation and tailored learning for women.

items.label: Support women’s entrepreneurship
items.summary: Consultation explicitly calls for support to women’s entrepreneurial initiatives and visible examples of existing initiatives.

items.label: Women’s participation in decision-making
items.summary: Consultation calls for stronger participation in decisions; the gender-impact report reiterates representation in decision-making bodies.

items.label: Services supporting work and family reconciliation
items.summary: The strategy records repeated requests for reconciliation of professional or working life and family life; it warns against treating this as women’s responsibility alone.

items.label: Equal pay, professional progression and entry into male-dominated sectors
items.summary: Responses identify unequal pay, glass ceilings and barriers to women’s employment in male-dominated sectors.

items.label: Equality and women’s empowerment activities
items.summary: The strategy calls for continuing equality-awareness and women’s empowerment activities.

items.label: Access to gender-violence services and shelters
items.summary: Women’s consultation responses identify improved access to gender-violence services, including shelters.

items.label: Childcare and care services for older people
items.summary: Responses call for childcare and older people’s day centres, home support and residences to improve reconciliation.

items.label: Employability training and mentoring
items.summary: Women’s consultation responses request vocational learning and mentoring that improves employability.

items.label: Challenge traditional gender roles and build carers’ networks
items.label_es: Roles de género y redes de cuidadoras
items.summary: Responses call for action against traditional gender roles, networks of carers and visibility of women acting as cultural facilitators.

items.label: Local training opportunities
items.summary: Consultation asks for more training options for young people in the territory.

items.label: Youth participation and associations
items.summary: Responses identify weak youth participation and the need to promote youth associations.

items.label: Youth spaces and diverse activities
items.summary: Consultation requests more spaces and infrastructure for varied activities by young people.

items.label: Housing access for young people
items.summary: Consultation requests better access to housing for young people.

items.label: Local young people as nature guides
items.summary: The strategy records a proposal to employ local young people as natural-environment guides.

items.label: Youth volunteering and environmental action
items.summary: Consultation requests volunteering and environmental-action programmes.

items.label: Vocational certificates and employment opportunities
items.summary: Consultation asks for employment-specific training and professional certificates, mentioning renewable-energy work, and rural employment placements.

items.label: Retain talent, support self-employment and remote work
items.summary: Responses identify youth emigration, a need to retain talent, incentives for self-employment and opportunities through remote work.

items.label: Sport, leisure and contemporary meeting places
items.label_es: Ocio, deporte y espacios de encuentro
items.summary: Youth consultation asks for gyms, cycle lanes, a covered sports hall and meeting places responding to current young people’s interests.

items.label: Youth in decision-making and visible local initiatives
items.summary: The youth-impact report seeks greater participation in decisions, public cultural/sport leisure services, social/environmental/cultural entrepreneurship and visibility of young people’s contribution.

items.label: Gender equality
items.summary: The strategy seeks women’s employment and entrepreneurship, representation in decisions, renewal of women’s associations, equality awareness and recognition of women’s local role.

items.label: Rural youth
items.summary: The strategy seeks youth participation, employment and enterprise opportunities, cultural/sport leisure and visibility of young people’s contribution.

items.label: Climate-change mitigation and adaptation
items.summary: The strategy seeks energy and water efficiency, a better emissions/sink balance, climate-adapted public spaces and proximity services, and conservation and enhancement of natural heritage.

CO.1.1.note: Count distinct prioritised needs actually addressed by the operation. Choose the appropriate exclusive CO.1 alternative yourself; selecting source references does not certify delivery or award points.

CO.1.2.note: Count distinct prioritised needs actually addressed by the operation. Choose the appropriate exclusive CO.1 alternative yourself; selecting source references does not certify delivery or award points.

CO.1.3.note: Count distinct prioritised needs actually addressed by the operation. Choose the appropriate exclusive CO.1 alternative yourself; selecting source references does not certify delivery or award points.

IN.1.1.note: No innovative economic sector is designated in this strategy edition. Existing manual claims are retained for review; no invented sector options are offered.

IN.1.2.note: Use the actual innovative-theme definition and explain the operation’s contribution. Multiple matching themes do not multiply IN.1.2 points.

IN.1.3.note: Check every condition in the chosen innovative aspect. Multiple references do not multiply IN.1.3 points.

IG.8.2.note: Document the women’s demand that the proposed activity addresses. The EDL records consultation interests rather than prescribing named leisure classes. Assess this exclusive subcriterion separately.

IG.11.7.note: Identify which documented women’s interest the meeting, workshop, forum or webinar addresses. Format alone does not establish the EDL connection.

DRI.3.3.note: Explain the at-risk group and specific need. These contextual references require an explicit link to the beneficiaries; no group or need is inferred from the project description.

JR.3.8.note: Explain the specific youth need addressed by the operation.

PT.1.2.note: Identify the traditional craft, work or food-related practice and the operation’s actual promotion, dissemination or conservation activity.

PT.1.3.note: Identify the rural-heritage interest and the operation’s actual contribution. The cited diagnosis is contextual evidence, not a list of automatically qualifying projects.

PS.1.2.note: Support both organisational membership and the organisation’s relevant stated objective.

LEADER-AL20-2.6.note: For rural-business diversification, consult the actual strategy and the operation’s funding-line conditions. An innovative theme or prioritised need does not establish eligibility by itself.
